title: Sprint-snap rollout heatmap and rollback cheatsheet — June 2026
content:
Purpose:
A compact, operational-first release pocket plan for the mid-sprint infra + runtime deployment that needs a fast canary and a one-click rollback path. Use this during the release window; keep it pinned in #release-ops.

High level summary:
- Target: runtime v1.14.2 (kernel optimizations + batching tweaks).
- Release window: 2026-06-16 01:00 UTC — 2026-06-16 04:00 UTC (low traffic slice).
- Risk profile: medium (kernel swap touching KV cache behavior).
- Goal: 15-minute canary, automated ramp to 50% in 45 minutes if metrics good; full rollout only after post-rollout acceptance.

Heatmap (deployment phases) — quick view:
- T-120m (2026-06-16 23:00 PDT): Final preflight checklist completed, release branch cut.
- T-60m (2026-06-16 00:00 PDT): Maintenance page prepared; cross-team readout.
- T-15m (2026-06-16 00:45 PDT): Dry-run smoke in staging; deploy job liveness check.
- T=0 (2026-06-16 01:00 UTC): Canary cluster receives 5% traffic for 15 minutes.
- T+15m: Evaluate canary, if ok -> 20% for next 20 minutes.
- T+35m: Evaluate -> 50% for 10 minutes.
- T+45m: Manual gate for 100% or continue progressive rollout to 100% over 30m.
- Post-100%: 2 hour observation window, then finalize release notes.

Pre-release checklist (must be green before T-60m):
- [ ] Release branch built and container images pushed (registry: ghcr.redwood-inference/runtime:v1.14.2).
- [ ] CI artifacts: integration tests passing on main branch (CI job ids included in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] DB migration: none in this release (confirm).
- [ ] Canary target nodes provisioned and tagged (tag: release-snap-2026-06).
- [ ] Load balancer route rule prepared with weight control (kubectl patch or infra UI verified).
- [ ] Rollback playbook open in browser and pinned in Slack.
- [ ] Pager roster confirmed for release window: oncall-sre, runtime-eng, release-engineer.
- [ ] Smoke test collection (smoke/smoke-suite-v2) available in /release/smoke/2026-06.

Canary plan (detailed):
- Canary allocation: 5% traffic to label: rollout_canary_2026_06_16.
- Canary duration: 15 minutes (short signal window to catch regressive latency/504s).
- Success criteria (all must be satisfied):
  - p95 latency delta <= +15% vs baseline (baseline: previous stable -> infra metrics 30d median).
  - Error rate (5xx) delta <= +0.1% absolute.
  - KV cache hit ratio not degraded by more than 3 percentage points.
  - Memory RSS of pod under 85% of limit for 10 minutes.
  - No new spike alerts triggered in alert manager: ALERT:runtime-high-err, ALERT:kv-cache-degradation.
- Canary observability commands (use during canary):
  - Prometheus query: rate(runtime_request_errors_total[5m]) and compare to baseline.
  - Grafana dashboard: runtime/latency-v1.14.2 (dashboard id: 1127).
  - k8s check: kubectl get pods -l app=runtime,rollout=canary -o wide.
  - Logs: gh logs --service runtime --since 15m --filter "level:ERROR"

Ramp schedule and decision gates (if any gate fails, rollback immediately):
- T+15m -> if all success criteria met: bump to 20% (automated). Else: stop & rollback.
- T+35m -> if 20% window OK: bump to 50%. If borderline (one metric slight exceed): hold for another 15m and re-evaluate.
- T+50m -> if 50% stable: schedule manual pause for 10m then proceed to 100% OR run longer observation at 50% if any signals are noisy.

Rollback quick paths (cheatsheet):
- Preferred fast rollback: rollback by weight -> route 100% back to stable tag (cli):
  - kubectl patch svc runtime-proxy -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"rollout":"stable"}}}'   # simple service selector swap (use infra UI if you prefer)
  - If using weight: curl -X POST https://infra-api.redwood-internal/rebalancer -d '{"service":"runtime","weights":{"stable":100}}'
- Full revert (if weight rollback failed): deploy previous image ghcr.redwood-inference/runtime:v1.14.1 to all nodes and restart.
- Emergency kill (worst-case): scale runtime deployment to zero and enable fallback lambda endpoints.
- Post-rollback checklist:
  - Validate user-facing errors cleared within 5 minutes.
  - Open a revert incident ticket and assign to oncall-sre.
  - Capture all IDs/logs, attach to JIRA REL-3241.

Smoke tests & acceptance (run these after a 100% rollout or after a rollback to verify recovery):
- smoke/smoke-suite-v2 -> run full list, expect 0 failures for critical flows.
- api-integration: ./scripts/run_api_checks.sh --env=prod --timeout=600
- End-to-end customers: run 5 synthetic multitenant sessions across regions (eu-west1, us-central1) and validate typical p95.

Telemetry and SLO checks (explicit queries):
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- error rate: sum(rate(runtime_request_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(runtime_requests_total[5m]))
- kv-cache-hit: increase(kv_cache_hit_total[10m]) / increase(kv_cache_lookup_total[10m])
- CPU saturation: sum(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total[5m])) by (pod) / sum(kube_pod_container_resource_limits_cpu_cores) by (pod)
- Alert thresholds (examples): p95 > 1200ms or error_rate > 0.5% -> page oncall-sre

Owners and immediate contacts (during window):
- Release owner: Marcus Chen (PM/Release-engineer) — slack @mchen
- Oncall SRE: Aisha Patel — pager duty PD-1423
- Runtime lead: Diego Ramirez — slack @dramirez
- Telemetry/observability: Sophie Lee — slack @sophie.lee

Escalation matrix (if no response within 10m):
- Ping primary on Slack, then call PD-1423. If still no response, escalate to Eng Director (R. Thompson).

Known risks and mitigations (short list):
- KV cache behavior: kernel optimization may change eviction pattern -> mitigation: short canary and KV metrics watch, keep cache warming job ready.
- Minor latency bump under heavy bursts: mitigation: set auto-throttle to conservative and monitor request queue length.
- Rare race in batcher shutdown path: mitigation: disable graceful drain on first rollout wave if observed and analyze logs.

Draft release notes (to be polished after final validation):
- Runtime v1.14.2: kernel-level batching improvements and KV cache performance tuning.
- Expected impact: up to 10% lower per-token latency for typical conversational workloads, reduced cost in median slices.
- No customer-facing schema or API changes.
- Known behavioral note: slight change to eviction heuristics for very long prefix workloads; flagged for investigation if customers report regressions.

Post-release tasks (owners):
- Release owner: finalize release notes and push to docs (docs team) within 4 hours.
- Runtime lead: open follow-up tasks for telemetry gaps or perf regressions within 24 hours.
- SRE: update oncall runbook with any new alerts; close temporary pages within 48 hours.

Open questions / TODOs before release:
- [ ] Confirm chaos tests not scheduled against canary nodes during window (ask infra).
- [ ] Verify auto-scaling cooldowns are 2m or less for the canary pool.
- [ ] Validate any dependent services (tokenizer) are pinned to compatible image (check INF-2870).

Notes and Quick links (for quick copy-paste during release):
- Patch service by selector: kubectl patch svc runtime-proxy -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"rollout":"stable"}}}'
- Weight change API: https://infra-api.redwood-internal/rebalancer
- Grafana dashboard id: 1127 (runtime/latency-v1.14.2)
- Slack channel: #release-ops (pin this doc)

Retrospective prompts (stamp these into the post-release review):
- Did the canary window (15m) give enough signal for KV cache changes?
- Were the success criteria tuned correctly (false positives/false negatives)?
- Which checks could be automated for next sprint?

-- end of pocket plan --

Revision history:
- 2026-06-10: initial draft by Marcus Chen.
- 2026-06-12: added ramp schedule and telemetry queries (Diego Ramirez).
- 2026-06-15: final preflight edits and rollback cheatsheet (Sophie Lee).
